rationale: Use the registered full reward from fixed R26, changing only native_rms_ratio from 0.33 to 0.2 to test weaker coordinate perturbations. Its stage-specific elite coordinate modes and affinity weights require selected teacher coordinates, stage assignment and scores; existing receptor/ligand geometry originates from the original common complex. Preserve distinct pointcloud alternatives rather than independently averaging feature targets into unsupported geometry. Endpoint pair-kernel and regional covariance associations motivate a geometric intervention, but neither establish that this family improves predicted pIC50 nor calibrate its weights. Retain registered component weights and the matched seed, steps and window. Introduce no increment target: supplied rates lack coordinate definitions and node support sufficient to specify one. Evaluate final predicted target pIC50 and secondary strain against unchanged R26. Compute spatial reward gradients through FLOWR endpoint VJP with detached correspondence; temporal derivatives are not spatial gradients. This is a bounded hypothesis, not an affinity-energy claim.
failure_modes: Lower native RMS may weaken useful steering and reduce final predicted target pIC50; the supplied associations do not predict this intervention outcome.
Teacher selection and affinity weighting may encode score bias; stage-specific target validity and transfer are untested.
Detached correspondence can switch between pointcloud matches or modes, causing discontinuous guidance; multimodal targets can still lose conformational diversity.
Untyped geometric contact or centre-distance terms can encourage collisions or strained conformations without improving chemical binding.
Whole-scalar rescaling can cancel under gradient normalization, whereas component reweighting changes direction; the selected update must control the actual native RMS perturbation.
Exploratory compressed evidence and absent node-level support cannot justify stage-specific reversals or a parent-child increment-matching objective.
